key_corrections: The 1960 teachers-union dispute has a late-Rhee prehistory: organizing attempts in 1958-1959 and a reported April 1959 Justice Ministry illegality interpretation must be recovered as a distinct predecessor document.
The dispute expanded beyond central ministries into Gyeongsangbuk-do personnel administration, administrative litigation and National Assembly legislation.
Gyeongbuk union claims of retaliatory transfer are evidence of the union's contemporaneous allegation, not by themselves proof of governmental motive.
The reported Daegu High Court suspension is interim judicial relief and must not be collapsed into a final merits judgment.
Post-May-16 arrests and revolutionary trials are a distinct military-regime suppression event, not a continuation of the same civilian-government decision.
Jo Jun-yeong (1960 Gyeongbuk governor) and Lee Jong-seok (1960 Gyeongnam teachers-union chair) require explicit same-name disambiguation controls.
